intent: Link to the previous page of a paged result set with a chevron and a short label.
typical_uses: The previous link at the start of the page row
Half of a previous/next pair with no page numbers

dont_use_when.situation: A previous-page action that is a state update with no URL of its own
A link to one numbered page
A link to the next page

invariants.text: The link renders a left chevron before the label and ignores children. With the default `text` its accessible name is "Go to previous page", set ahead of the consumer's props. A custom `text` is the name instead, since the visible label is hidden below 640px and the chevron is decorative; an empty or blank `text`, the icon-only form, keeps "Go to previous page". An `aria-label` passed to it replaces either.
The visible label is hidden below a 640px viewport width (pagination.module.css `.previousNextText`), so a narrow viewport shows the chevron alone.
The chevron is mirrored under a right-to-left direction (pagination.module.css `.chevron:dir(rtl)`), so it keeps pointing toward the previous pages whatever the reading direction.

anti_patterns.dont: Pass an `aria-label` that leaves out the words of a custom `text`
anti_patterns.do_instead: Leave `aria-label` off, so the name follows `text`; when you do override it, keep the visible words in it, or a voice-control user who says what is on screen cannot press the link

a11y.by: pagination.test.tsx asserts getByRole('link', { name: 'Go to previous page' }) finds the link with the default `text`, whose visible label is "Previous", that a custom `text` "Forward" is the name instead, that an `aria-label` passed to it wins over either, and that an empty or blank `text` keeps "Go to previous page"

rtl.by: pagination.module.css mirrors the chevron with `.chevron:dir(rtl)` and pagination.test.tsx pins that rule, but jsdom has no layout and does not resolve `:dir()`, so no suite renders the link right-to-left

unexposed_parts.reason: pagination.tsx renders a ChevronLeftIcon inside the link; it is not exported as a component of its own and cannot be replaced.
pagination.tsx renders `text` in a span with the stylesheet's previousNextText class; it is not exported, and `text` is the only control over it.

good.title: A custom label, which is also the accessible name
A longer name that keeps the visible word in it

bad.title: A name that drops the visible word
bad.why: The name no longer contains "Newer", so a voice-control user who says the word they see on screen cannot press the link.

bad.title: A label given as children
bad.why: The link renders fixed content and ignores children; the visible label is set through `text`.
